newsitem.title: UK: LME base metals mostly stable, but nickel easier.
newsitem.headline: LME base metals mostly stable, but nickel easier.

text.p: The base metals markets were generally stable in slow inter-office trading on Thursday, with LME stock drops in copper and aluminium helping stop an early downward drift.
Nickel, however, ticked lower and analysts said it was on shaky technical territory after the sharp sell-off this week.
Prices were approaching recent support at $7,230, the low from April 30. It was last indicated at $7,235/$7,250, compared to Wednesday's kerb finish of $7,280.
Chartists said a downside break would target $7,110, but traders noted that the downside could be limited initially.
"It's encountered some light selling this morning but I can't see it much lower than $7,200 today at which point some scale-down buying will be the order of the day," a trader said.
The market was watching labour talks at Inco Ltd's Sudbury, Ontario operations ahead of the May 31 contract expiry, although so far the talks have had little supportive value.
The union representing 4,700 Inco workers said late on Wednesday that it had rejected the nickel miner's latest contract offer.
Earlier in the week the union had requested the help of a mediator after talks stalled.
Meanwhile, three-months copper was trading $2 up from Wednesday's close at $2,533 per tonne, after initially sliding below the $2,530 support level.
"The LME stock draw of 3,550 tonnes helped turn that around. It's quite supportive," a trader said.
"But the market is overbought and I can't see copper do more than range-trade today."
Cash to threes backwardation was also higher at $77/82, compared to $73/$78.
A similar scenario prevailed in aluminium, which was slightly easier but supported by a stock decline of 3,700 tonnes.
Prices were last indicated slightly lower at $1,640/42, versus $1,645 at Wednesday's kerb close.
Zinc prices looked set to consolidate betwen the recent high of $1,370 and support at $1,350, traders said. It was barely changed at $1,357/$1,359.
Lacking any upward impetus, tin ticked down to the nearby support level of $5,630/40, compared to $5,665, while lead was $2 lower at $639.
Alloy was indicated virtually unchanged at $1,500/$1,510.
